issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify the attribute 'lectureName' as type String, but the solution introduces a new LectureName class and declares the field as 'private LectureName lectureName'. This creates an attribute type mismatch across artifacts and introduces an unexpected additional class not mentioned in the exercise. Students expecting to work with a String (per UML and exercise text) will be confused and unable to reconcile the different types.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the lectureName type across all artifacts. Either revert the solution to use a String field (private String lectureName) and remove the LectureName class, adjusting constructor/getters/setters accordingly, or update the problem statement and template to document and use the LectureName type throughout (including UML, constructor signature, and getter/setter types).

issues.description: The constructor signature in the solution takes a LectureName as the first parameter, while the problem statement and UML expect lectureName to be a String. This constructor parameter type differs from the specification and will prevent students from following the intended constructor design.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor parameter types consistent with the specification. Change the solution constructor to accept a String for lectureName (or update the problem/template to require a LectureName type). Ensure the parameter order matches the UML (lectureName first, then the integer attributes).

issues.description: The solution's getter and setter for lectureName declare String types (getLectureName(): String, setLectureName(String)), but the backing field is LectureName. The getter returns the LectureName field and the setter assigns a String to it, causing a type/return mismatch and a compile error. This internal inconsistency in the solution breaks the expected method signatures and behavior described in the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure getter/setter signatures match the field type. Either change the field to 'private String lectureName' so getLectureName()/setLectureName(String) operate on String, or change the getter/setter to use LectureName (getLectureName(): LectureName, setLectureName(LectureName)) and update the problem statement/template accordingly.

issues.description: The problem statement and template describe the lectureName attribute as a String (attribute named 'lectureName'), but the solution introduces a new type/identifier LectureName and declares the lectureName field and constructor parameter using LectureName. This introduces a different identifier for the same conceptual entity (the lecture's name) across artifacts and creates confusion for students mapping the requirement (a String lectureName) to the solution implementation (a LectureName object).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the representation of the lecture name consistent across artifacts. Either (A) revert the solution to use a String for lectureName (change the field and constructor parameter to String and remove the LectureName class), or (B) update the problem statement and template to explicitly introduce and use the LectureName type (and adjust method signatures accordingly). Prefer option (A) to match the stated exercise requirements (lectureName: String).
